yyoreel never collects media, frames, screenshots, browser data, URLs, paths, code, prompts, accounts, email, IP-derived IDs, free text, or raw user data.

## Step types

Each step has an `action` field. Most steps accept optional `label`, `delay` (ms after step), and `description` fields.

| Action       | Key fields                                  | Purpose                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `pause`      | `ms`                                        | Wait for a duration                |
| `click`      | `text` or `selector`, `within`, `modifiers` | Click an element                   |
| `type`       | `text`, `selector`, `within`, `charDelay`   | Type text into an input            |
| `key`        | `key`, `target`                             | Press a key combo (e.g. `"cmd+s"`) |
| `drag`       | `from`, `to` (element targets)              | Drag between two elements          |
| `scroll`     | `x`, `y`, `selector`                        | Scroll the page or an element      |
| `wheel`      | `deltaY`, `deltaX`, `count`, element target | Dispatch real mouse wheel events   |
| `wait`       | `selector` or `text`, `timeout`             | Wait for an element to appear      |
| `moveTo`     | `text` or `selector`, `within`              | Move cursor to an element          |
| `navigate`   | `url`                                       | Navigate to a new URL              |
| `hover`      | `text` or `selector`, `within`              | Hover over an element              |
| `select`     | `selector`, `value`                         | Select a dropdown value            |
| `screenshot` | `output`                                    | Capture a PNG screenshot           |

For full field details on every step type, see [steps-reference.md](steps-reference.md).

## Element targeting

Many steps target elements using these fields:

- `text` - match by visible text content
- `selector` - match by CSS selector
- `within` - narrow the search to a parent matching this CSS selector

You can use `text` or `selector` (not both). `within` is optional and scopes the search.

```json
{ "action": "click", "text": "Submit" }
{ "action": "click", "selector": "#submit-btn" }
{ "action": "click", "text": "Submit", "within": ".modal" }
```

## Viewport presets

Use preset names as string values for `viewport`, or specify `{ width, height }`. Both forms override automatic display sizing:

`desktop` (1920x1080), `desktop-hd` (2560x1440), `laptop` (1366x768), `macbook-air` (1440x900), `macbook-pro` (1512x982), `ipad` (1024x1366), `ipad-pro` (834x1194), `ipad-mini` (768x1024), `iphone-15` (393x852), `iphone-15-pro-max` (430x932), `iphone-se` (375x667), `pixel-8` (412x915), `galaxy-s24` (360x780).

## Theme

Customize the recording background, cursor appearance, and keystroke HUD:

```json
{
  "theme": {
    "background": "#8b5cf6",
    "cursor": {
      "image": "./cursor.svg",
      "size": 32,
      "hotspot": "center",
      "animationStyle": "medium"
    },
    "hud": {
      "enabled": true,
      "background": "rgba(30, 41, 59, 0.85)",
      "color": "#e2e8f0",
      "fontSize": 48,
      "fontFamily": "\"SF Mono\", monospace",
      "borderRadius": 12,
      "position": "top"
    }
  }
}
```

- `background` - `"none"` (default), a hex color (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`), or a readable local image path; colors and images create a centered rounded inset with a shadow, while the HUD remains at canvas level
- `cursor.image` - path to a custom cursor SVG or PNG; the contrast-safe built-in Icons8 arrow uses a white fill with a black outline and stays visible through hover and click press; custom cursor artwork also remains unchanged while clicking; press and release use a 100ms cubic ease-out scale transition that reaches `0.75` at full press
- `cursor.size` - cursor size in pixels
- `cursor.hotspot` - `"top-left"` (default) or `"center"` for custom images; the built-in arrow uses its calibrated intrinsic hotspot
- `cursor.animationStyle` - `"smooth"`, `"medium"` (default), `"rapid"`, or `"none"`; only these named presets are accepted
- `hud.enabled` - `true` (default) to show the keystroke and shortcut HUD; set to `false` to omit it from previews, timelines, and all recorded output formats
- `hud.position` - `"top"` or `"bottom"`

## Common patterns

### Shared steps via include

Factor out reusable step sequences (e.g. dismissing a cookie banner) into JSON files:

```json
// steps/dismiss-banner.json
{
  "steps": [
    { "action": "wait", "selector": ".cookie-banner", "timeout": 5000 },
    { "action": "click", "selector": ".accept-btn", "delay": 300 }
  ]
}
```

Reference them in the config:

```json
{
  "include": ["./steps/dismiss-banner.json"],
  "videos": { ... }
}
```

### Multiple videos in one config

Define several videos in the `videos` map. Shared settings (`viewport`, `theme`, `defaultDelay`) are inherited from the top level. If neither level sets `viewport`, each recording uses automatic display sizing.

### Environment variables

Config values support `$VAR` and `${VAR}` substitution from the environment.

`YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` is process control, not config substitution. Keep it out
of `yyoreel.config.json` and set it on the `record` or `preview` process.

### Output formats

Set the `output` extension to control format: `.mp4` (default), `.gif`, `.webm`.

```json
{ "output": "demo.gif" }
```

## Tips

- Always set `waitFor` on a video to ensure the page is ready before steps run.
- Use `delay` on individual steps to control pacing between actions.
- Use `--watch` during development for automatic re-recording on config changes.
- Use `composite` to iterate on theme/overlay settings without re-recording.
- Use `--verbose` to debug step execution.
- Use `--dry-run` to inspect the resolved viewport, configured values, includes, environment substitutions, and steps.
- Use `zoom` to scale up small UIs for readability in the recording.
- Cap-style autozoom is enabled by default for recordings. It runs after static `zoom`, transforms the complete recording card and cursor over a fixed background, merges related clicks, re-aims after meaningful cursor movement, and keeps the keystroke HUD screen-fixed. Use `autoZoom: false` to disable it.
- Use `theme.background` to present the recording as a polished inset on a solid color or local image. Image paths resolve relative to the config file.
- Start with `preview` to verify steps work before committing to a full recording.

## Shared-browser mistakes

- Starting isolated Chrome when the calling tool already exposes CDP. Reuse the
  existing endpoint.
- Setting `WEBREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`. Use `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`.
- Killing Chrome after an attached run. yyoreel owns only its dedicated target.
- Treating viewport emulation as browser-window resizing. Judge the recorded
  dimensions, not the shared window's outer size.
- Reporting success from command exit alone. Decode the output and verify the
  provider browser is still healthy.

## Reference files

- [steps-reference.md](steps-reference.md) - detailed docs for all 12 step types
- [examples.md](examples.md) - annotated config examples for common use cases
# Browser and credential ownership audit

Date: 2026-10-03. Read-only source review against Hermes commit `f97608f178d1ffeca59860195ab7da295f7c8e5f`, verified with `git rev-parse HEAD` in `.local/hermes-lab/upstream`. Sources below are relative to that upstream checkout. No real credentials, browser sessions, model calls, network calls, or upstream edits were used. Temporary-home probes used dummy values and mocked the browser socket boundary.

## Verdict

**A single Hermes profile serving two private Slack users and a shared thread does not provide the required private browser/credential ownership boundary. This is demonstrated behavior, not merely an untested fear.** Separate conversation IDs do not separate the local vault; named Browser Use sessions and persistent Camofox identities are also shared within a profile. This does not mean data spontaneously leaks on every normal request, nor that every deployment fails. The local baseline has not configured or run the intended browser deployment yet.

**Separate routed profiles do provide useful logical separation for the local vault, external-manager unlock tokens, Browser Use backend cache keys, and managed Camofox identities.** They are worth reusing. They are not sufficient evidence of an adversarial runtime boundary: `browser_exec` explicitly runs arbitrary host Python, and the real-profile browser has a process-global CDP cache that is not keyed by profile. Disable that optional real-profile path in a shared process unless fixed/isolated. Whole-runtime isolation is one solution; a restricted browser service and tightly limited tools is another. An unconditional permanent instance per user is not proved necessary by this audit.

## Request identity into the browser

1. `gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1688-1726` passes the gateway conversation's `ctx.session_id` as `task_id` to `agent.run_conversation`; it separately passes `ctx.source.user_id` as `turn_author.id`. Browser ownership is therefore not automatically the Slack sender identity.
2. `tools/browser_use_cli.py:812-819` takes `task_id` from tool-dispatch kwargs, but accepts `session` from model tool arguments. Its schema describes an omitted session as the shared default (`789-803`).
3. The backend key is `bu-named-{session}` if a name is supplied, otherwise the task ID. A served-profile tag is appended when a home override is active (`364-376`). Two different conversations in the same profile using `session="work"` get the same backend key. Two distinct profiles get different backend keys.
4. The CLI receives `BU_NAME=session` directly (`630-645`). For shared CDP browsers it adds an own-tab preamble, which is a best-effort concurrency measure, not a cookie/context authorization boundary (`38-74`). Documentation explicitly says the omitted session uses a shared default daemon (`website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md:72-90`). This audit did not independently inspect/run the external Browser Use daemon, so its entire IPC isolation contract is not certified here.
5. Built-in browser tools do better at task binding: `_get_session_info` indexes runtime sessions by task ID and stores owner metadata (`tools/browser_tool_session.py:346-399`); `_last_session_key` checks the recorded owner before non-navigation tools reuse a binding (`tools/browser_tool.py:335-359`). This protects ordinary routing from stale/wrong task bindings. It does not give per-owner account isolation when the chosen backend intentionally shares cookies/browser state.

## Browser backend distinctions

| Path | Actual isolation/reuse behavior | Implication for two DMs plus shared thread |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clean built-in local Chromium | Fresh random browser session name for each runtime task; real-profile off gives a clean session (`browser_tool_session.py:243-271`). | Separate task IDs normally separate initial browsers. No persistent owner login guarantee follows from that alone. |
| Browserbase | Creates a new remote session using project config; no persistent context ID is in its create payload (`plugins/browser/browserbase/provider.py:64-101`). | Ordinary task session separation is real. Named Browser Use session-key reuse can intentionally reuse a cached browser within the same profile. |
| Browser Use provider / Nous managed provider | Creates `/browsers` session; direct payload is `{}`, managed payload is timeout/proxy country, with task-derived idempotency for managed mode (`plugins/browser/browser_use/provider.py:129-159`). | Do not infer owner-scoped persistent cloud profiles merely from vendor support. The reviewed create payload does not supply a per-owner persistent profile ID. |
| Firecrawl | Creates `/v2/browser` with TTL and receives a CDP URL (`plugins/browser/firecrawl/provider.py:53-68`). | Fresh provider session machinery, with the same task/name cache caveats. |
| Camofox, default ephemeral | Random user identity for each new runtime task (`tools/browser_camofox.py:265-280`). | Different tasks initially differ. Real server isolation remains a provider/server acceptance check. |
| Camofox managed persistence | Stable `user_id` from Hermes profile path; distinct task IDs alter only `session_key` (`tools/browser_camofox_state.py:16-27`). | All users sharing one Hermes profile intentionally share the persistent Camofox identity/cookies. Separate owner profiles generate separate identities. |
| Camofox explicit external identity | Configured `user_id` overrides generated identities; a configured session key may also be shared (`tools/browser_camofox.py:176-183,265-280`). | The operator must give each authorized context its own external identity. This is not derived from Slack identity. |
| CDP override (`browser.cdp_url` or `BROWSER_CDP_URL`) | Overrides cloud/local session creation (`tools/browser_tool_session.py:332-343`). `BROWSER_CDP_URL` is a process-environment lookup, then profile config (`tools/browser_tool_cdp.py:51-60`). | All tasks using the same endpoint share the browser's authority. Separate tabs do not separate cookies or logged-in accounts. A process-global endpoint is unsuitable for private owner boundaries. |
| Real-profile toggle | Copies the host OS user's active Chromium-family profile and drives it. The live CDP cache is one global `"cdp"` slot (`tools/browser_tool.py:261-266`, `tools/browser_tool_real_profile.py:226-261`). | Same-profile tasks share the user's logged-in browser by design. Across profiles in one process, both with real-profile enabled, the cached endpoint can also be reused before checking the second profile's copy directory. |

The provider-selection/config caches themselves are profile-aware (`tools/browser_tool_cloud.py:21-33,45-73`). That is a useful existing guarantee; it does not override the separate real-profile cache issue.

Hermes's own docs describe real-profile browsing as a convenience rather than an isolation boundary (`website/docs/user-guide/features/browser.md:258-265`). The docs explicitly say managed Camofox persistence is profile-scoped and requires server-side support (`391-421`). The broad overview line that every task has a session must be read with these distinctions (`29-34`).

## Vault: what it protects, and what it does not

The credential vault **exists at the audited pinned commit**. It is not a feature assumed from a newer branch.

- The local encrypted store is `<get_hermes_home()>/vault`, with a key and encrypted file. Item metadata contains ID, kind, label, origin, identifier and dates, but no Slack user/owner or conversation audience field (`agent/vault_store.py:153-173,193-201,355-375`).
- `browser_vault_list` walks all enabled backends and returns every available item’s non-secret metadata; it receives no authenticated owner input (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:221-259,710-711`). A local backend is always included (`agent/vault_backends/base.py:125-139`).
- `browser_vault_fill` accepts a handle, resolves it in the current profile’s backends, checks the saved origin, then injects into the current task’s browser. It does not check the Slack sender or require that the task that saved the item is the one using it (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:400-479,521-569`). This is the correct design for one personal profile reused across its owner's sessions, but not for several independent owners in one profile.
- Passwords are withheld from ordinary model tool outputs. Exact-origin checks, an in-page recheck, server-side secret injection, and redaction are real protections. **These protect password handling; they do not authorize which human may use the account.** Someone can improperly act through a login without seeing the password.
- External password-manager unlock tokens are keyed by `(Hermes home, backend)` (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:65-104`). The `owner_session` field only decides which session teardown removes the token (`113-141`); it is not checked when another session fetches the token. Same-profile sessions can reuse an existing unlock. Different-profile tokens are separated.
- 1Password service tokens and Connect credentials use the current profile's secret scope; the configured account may differ by profile (`agent/vault_backends/onepassword.py:36-40,50-68`). Managers list login items available to their configured manager account rather than applying a Slack-owner filter (`101-124`; `agent/vault_backends/bitwarden.py:88-124`). Bitwarden’s CLI home/appdata environment comes from the host (`28-29,48-53`), so separate token slots do not by themselves configure distinct Bitwarden accounts for separate reviewers.

The docs accurately state local vault scope is the profile (`website/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault.md:87-90`), and describe the model-blind origin-binding guarantee (`110-122`). They do not promise per-Slack-user account authorization.

## Related secure input finding

Messaging `gateway/` contains no registration of the vault unlock/save-login/code callbacks. Registration exists in CLI chat and TUI/Desktop bridges (`hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py:312-319`; `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:216-232`). The messaging turn runner registers the ordinary gateway approval callback, not these vault callbacks (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1688-1728`). `can_prompt_here()` requires the vault unlock callback (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:162-171`). Therefore stock Slack should not be assumed to have the documented masked credential dialog. Saved local credentials can still be used by that profile. A secure web handoff or an appropriate callback bridge is needed for the reviewer collection experience; no new vault cryptography is implied.

## Local probes and limits

Reproducible source: [probes/browser_vault_ownership.py](probes/browser_vault_ownership.py). Captured successful invocation and output: [evidence/browser_vault_ownership.json](evidence/browser_vault_ownership.json).

A temporary Python process created three disposable Hermes homes, disabled external managers in dummy config, and used real imports. Dummy records were added through `VaultStore.add_item`; list and fill functions were the real implementations. Only page inspection/injection functions were mocked to prevent browser/network use. It checked these outcomes, all true:

| Probe | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| DM-B task lists DM-A dummy vault metadata in same profile | Allowed |
| DM-B reaches the secret-fill boundary using A's handle on the matching dummy origin | Allowed; injection received B's task ID and A's dummy secret |
| Different profile lists A's local vault entry | Denied by separate store; list empty |
| DM-B reuses A's dummy Bitwarden token in same profile | Allowed |
| Different profile reuses A's dummy manager token | No token |
| Different task IDs plus same named Browser Use session within a profile | Same backend cache key |
| Same name under different profile homes | Different backend cache keys |
| Unnamed Browser Use backend keys for different task IDs | Different keys; this does not certify external harness default-daemon isolation |
| Camofox managed identities for A/B tasks in one profile | Same user ID, different session keys |
| Camofox managed identities under different profiles | Different user IDs |
| Real-profile cached CDP endpoint queried under profile A then B, both enabled | Same endpoint returned |

The real-profile probe pre-seeded a dummy cached endpoint and mocked healthcheck/socket-directory preparation. It demonstrates the profile-unkeyed cache path, not a live cross-account browser theft. The vault fill probe demonstrates the missing owner check and successful traversal to the injection boundary, not successful login to a real website. No live Slack/browser E2E has been completed by these probes.

Relevant existing upstream tests cover exact-origin rejection, secret-free return values, race rechecks and file guards (`tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py`), profile-scoped external token storage and teardown ownership (`tests/agent/test_vault_backends.py:139-170`), and profile-keyed Browser Use backend caches (`tests/tools/test_browser_computer_use_profile_cache_keys.py:28-46`). Their intended assertions do not establish two-user authorization inside one profile.

## Smallest justified next design

1. Route each authenticated owner’s private DM to its own Hermes profile; route shared channels/threads to a separate audience profile without private owner credentials. Reuse native profile vaults and secret scopes. This establishes logical ownership for the reviewed profile-scoped paths.
2. Force browser session names/identities from trusted runtime context rather than model-chosen owner/session IDs. A thin integration can namespace each logical browser session by the authorized profile and owner; a browser service can reject any foreign identifier. Keep private persistent browser contexts separately bound to that authority.
3. Keep `browser.use_real_profile` off in the shared process; avoid a shared/global CDP endpoint. Use explicitly isolated browser contexts/services or fix the real-profile cache and prove the relevant backend behavior. Camofox persistence can reuse owner profile identities if its server truly enforces them.
4. Decide the execution boundary from enabled capabilities. `browser_exec` runs arbitrary **host** Python (`model_tools.py:391-395`; its actual dispatch is a host subprocess in `tools/browser_use_cli.py:612-662`). A Docker-only terminal setting does not establish isolation for this path. Options include whole-runtime OS/container isolation, or disabling host-code-capable tools and using a constrained browser broker plus storage/credential ACLs. Merely naming profiles is insufficient for hostile direct resource attempts.
5. Test two private owners plus one shared audience with dummy markers against those exact tools and settings, including named browser-session collision, matching-origin foreign vault use, persistent cookies, same-process profile transitions, concurrent actions, and restart. Treat only verified backend behavior as accepted.

**Verified outcome: stock same-profile browser/vault scope fails the requested private-owner boundary; routed profiles reuse substantial existing machinery, but the selected browser and execution path still require explicit enforcement and live acceptance.**

# yyoreel

yyoreel records scripted browser demos as MP4, GIF, or WebM with cursor animation, keystroke overlays, and sound effects. You define steps in a JSON config, and yyoreel drives headless Chrome, captures frames, and encodes with ffmpeg.

## Agent browser contract

Choose one browser mode before running `record` or `preview`:

1. If the calling environment, browser wrapper, yyork, d3k, or another tool
   provides a CDP endpoint, attach to it with `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`.
2. Otherwise, let yyoreel download and launch its isolated Chrome.

Shared Chrome is the preferred mode whenever it is already available. Use the
provider's documented status or endpoint command. Do not guess a port, start a
second Chrome, add a browser field to the yyoreel config, or translate the
endpoint into CLI flags.

Pass the endpoint only to the yyoreel process:

```bash
YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT="$cdp_endpoint" yyoreel record -c yyoreel.config.json
```

If a wrapper already injects `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`, invoke the wrapper as
documented instead of exporting another value. `WEBREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` is the
obsolete pre-rename variable and has no effect.

Attach mode creates a dedicated page target. yyoreel may close that target, but
the agent must leave the browser process and every other target running. The
configured viewport uses device emulation on yyoreel's target. It does not
resize the shared browser window.

After recording:

1. Confirm the output exists and decode it with `ffprobe` or `ffmpeg`.
2. Confirm the provider still reports its browser or CDP endpoint as healthy.
3. Report the output path and whether the shared browser survived.

## Prerequisites

Use Node.js 20.20+ on the 20.x line, or 22.22 and later.

yyoreel requires Chrome and ffmpeg. In isolated launch mode, both are automatically downloaded to `~/.yyoreel` on first run if not already present. Do not install Chrome or Chromium via puppeteer, playwright, or another browser automation tool.

In attach mode, yyoreel uses the existing Chrome and skips its Chrome download
and launch path. ffmpeg is still required for recording and composition.

To download dependencies explicitly, or to fix corrupted/broken binaries:

```bash
yyoreel install
yyoreel install --force   # delete cached binaries and re-download
```

To override the auto-downloaded binaries, set these environment variables:

- `CHROME_PATH` - path to a Chrome or Chromium binary (used for preview)
- `CHROME_HEADLESS_PATH` - path to a chrome-headless-shell binary (used for recording)
- `FFMPEG_PATH` - path to an ffmpeg binary
- `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` - existing Chrome remote debugging HTTP endpoint, WebSocket debugger URL, or port

When `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` is set, yyoreel skips Chrome download and launch,
creates a dedicated page target in the attached browser, and closes only that
target after the run. The browser remains running. The configured viewport uses
device emulation on the target and does not resize the existing browser window.
Recording features, including capture pacing, Retina quality, autozoom,
backgrounds, cursor overlays, and the HUD, use the same pipeline as launch mode.

If attach mode fails before the first step, verify the provider's endpoint is
reachable and that the wrapper passed `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`. If the browser
connects but a step fails, inspect `waitFor`, selectors, page timing, and
`--verbose` output.

## CLI commands

### init

Scaffold a new `yyoreel.config.json`.

```bash
yyoreel init
yyoreel init --name login-flow --url https://myapp.com
yyoreel init --name hero -o hero.config.json
```

Flags: `--name` (video name), `--url` (starting URL), `-o, --output` (output file path).

### record

Record one or more videos.

```bash
yyoreel record                        # all videos in config
yyoreel record hero login             # specific videos by name
yyoreel record -c custom.config.json  # custom config path
yyoreel record --watch                # re-record on config change
yyoreel record --verbose              # log each step
yyoreel record --dry-run              # print resolved config only
yyoreel record --frames               # save raw PNGs to .yyoreel/frames/
```

To record through an existing Chrome:

```bash
YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9222 yyoreel record hero
```

### preview

Run steps in a visible browser without recording.

```bash
yyoreel preview
yyoreel preview hero --verbose
```

### composite

Re-apply the recording background and overlays (cursor, HUD, sfx) to existing raw video without re-recording. Useful for tweaking theme settings.

```bash
yyoreel composite
yyoreel composite hero
```

### install

Download Chrome and ffmpeg to `~/.yyoreel`. Also use this to fix corrupted or broken binaries.

```bash
yyoreel install
yyoreel install --force  # delete cached binaries and re-download
```

### validate

Check config for errors without running anything.

```bash
yyoreel validate
yyoreel validate -c custom.config.json
```

## Config structure

Config files are auto-discovered as `yyoreel.config.json` (or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, `.mjs`). Use `-c` to specify a custom path.

### Top-level fields

| Field          | Default      | Description                                             |
| -------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `$schema`      | -            | `"https://yyoreel.com/schema/v1.json"`                  |
| `outDir`       | `"videos/"`  | Output directory for rendered videos                    |
| `baseUrl`      | `""`         | Base URL prepended to relative video URLs               |
| `viewport`     | main display | Usable logical area on macOS, with a 1080x1080 fallback |
| `theme`        | -            | Recording background, cursor, and HUD theme             |
| `sfx`          | -            | Sound effect settings                                   |
| `include`      | -            | Array of step file paths prepended to all videos        |
| `defaultDelay` | -            | Default delay (ms) appended after each step             |
| `clickDwell`   | -            | Cursor dwell time (ms) before a click                   |

### Per-video fields

Each entry in the `videos` map supports:

| Field          | Default        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`          | required       | URL to open (absolute or relative to `baseUrl`)    |
| `viewport`     | inherited      | Explicit dimensions or preset override             |
| `zoom`         | -              | CSS zoom factor                                    |
| `autoZoom`     | `true`         | Spring-zoom the card around related clicks         |
| `waitFor`      | -              | Selector or text to wait for before starting steps |
| `output`       | `"<name>.mp4"` | Output path (`.mp4`, `.gif`, `.webm`)              |
| `thumbnail`    | `{ time: 0 }`  | Thumbnail config, or `{ enabled: false }`          |
| `include`      | inherited      | Step files to prepend                              |
| `theme`        | inherited      | Override theme                                     |
| `sfx`          | inherited      | Override sound effects                             |
| `defaultDelay` | inherited      | Override default delay                             |
| `clickDwell`   | inherited      | Override click dwell                               |
| `fps`          | `60`           | Frame rate                                         |
| `quality`      | `80`           | Final quality and 1x or 2x physical pixel density  |
| `steps`        | required       | Array of step objects                              |

When `viewport` is omitted on macOS, yyoreel uses the main display's usable area in logical CSS pixels. Unsupported or display-less environments fall back to 1080x1080. An explicit object or named preset overrides automatic sizing.

Quality values from 80 through 100 keep the resolved CSS viewport and double the physical output width and height. Values from 1 through 79 use 1x output dimensions. If a 1x viewport has an odd dimension, yyoreel keeps its CSS layout and pads that output edge by one pixel for compatible 4:2:0 video. Automatic viewport discovery does not override this mapping. The default quality matches native density on a 2x Retina display, but density always comes from `quality`. Chrome supplies lossless PNG screencast frames. During capture, yyoreel remuxes those frames so video encoding cannot slow the output clock. Once capture stops, it compacts the retained raw with lossless ultrafast QP0 H.264 RGB while preserving the source RGB samples. A fixed output clock reuses the latest source frame when necessary to maintain the requested frame rate. For MP4 output, the final H.264 encode is the only lossy generation, using the quality-to-CRF mapping, the `veryfast` preset, and compatible 4:2:0 output. WebM and GIF exports apply their format-specific delivery encode after composition.

## Vault: what it protects, and what it does not

The credential vault **exists at the audited pinned commit**. It is not a feature assumed from a newer branch.

- The local encrypted store is `<get_hermes_home()>/vault`, with a key and encrypted file. Item metadata contains ID, kind, label, origin, identifier and dates, but no Slack user/owner or conversation audience field (`agent/vault_store.py:153-173,193-201,355-375`).
- `browser_vault_list` walks all enabled backends and returns every available item’s non-secret metadata; it receives no authenticated owner input (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:221-259,710-711`). A local backend is always included (`agent/vault_backends/base.py:125-139`).
- `browser_vault_fill` accepts a handle, resolves it in the current profile’s backends, checks the saved origin, then injects into the current task’s browser. It does not check the Slack sender or require that the task that saved the item is the one using it (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:400-479,521-569`). This is the correct design for one personal profile reused across its owner's sessions, but not for several independent owners in one profile.
- Passwords are withheld from ordinary model tool outputs. Exact-origin checks, an in-page recheck, server-side secret injection, and redaction are real protections. **These protect password handling; they do not authorize which human may use the account.** Someone can improperly act through a login without seeing the password.
- External password-manager unlock tokens are keyed by `(Hermes home, backend)` (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:65-104`). The `owner_session` field only decides which session teardown removes the token (`113-141`); it is not checked when another session fetches the token. Same-profile sessions can reuse an existing unlock. Different-profile tokens are separated.
- 1Password service tokens and Connect credentials use the current profile's secret scope; the configured account may differ by profile (`agent/vault_backends/onepassword.py:36-40,50-68`). Managers list login items available to their configured manager account rather than applying a Slack-owner filter (`101-124`; `agent/vault_backends/bitwarden.py:88-124`). Bitwarden’s CLI home/appdata environment comes from the host (`28-29,48-53`), so separate token slots do not by themselves configure distinct Bitwarden accounts for separate reviewers.

The docs accurately state local vault scope is the profile (`website/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault.md:87-90`), and describe the model-blind origin-binding guarantee (`110-122`). They do not promise per-Slack-user account authorization.

Messaging `gateway/` contains no registration of the vault unlock/save-login/code callbacks. Registration exists in CLI chat and TUI/Desktop bridges (`hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py:312-319`; `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:216-232`). Therefore stock Slack should not be assumed to have the documented masked credential dialog. Saved local credentials can still be used by that profile. ## Smallest justified next design

1. Route each authenticated owner’s private DM to its own Hermes profile; route shared channels/threads to a separate audience profile without private owner credentials. Reuse native profile vaults and secret scopes. This establishes logical ownership for the reviewed profile-scoped paths.
2. Force browser session names/identities from trusted runtime context rather than model-chosen owner/session IDs. A thin integration can namespace each logical browser session by the authorized profile and owner; a browser service can reject any foreign identifier. Keep private persistent browser contexts separately bound to that authority.
3. Keep `browser.use_real_profile` off in the shared process; avoid a shared/global CDP endpoint. Use explicitly isolated browser contexts/services or fix the real-profile cache and prove the relevant backend behavior. Camofox persistence can reuse owner profile identities if its server truly enforces them.
4. Decide the execution boundary from enabled capabilities. `browser_exec` runs arbitrary **host** Python (`model_tools.py:391-395`; its actual dispatch is a host subprocess in `tools/browser_use_cli.py:612-662`). A Docker-only terminal setting does not establish isolation for this path. Options include whole-runtime OS/container isolation, or disabling host-code-capable tools and using a constrained browser broker plus storage/credential ACLs. Merely naming profiles is insufficient for hostile direct resource attempts.
5. Test two private owners plus one shared audience with dummy markers against those exact tools and settings, including named browser-session collision, matching-origin foreign vault use, persistent cookies, same-process profile transitions, concurrent actions, and restart. Treat only verified backend behavior as accepted.

# AGENTS.md

- Use the latest versions of npm packages when adding dependencies.
- Never use emojis in code, comments, documentation, or commit messages.
- When making user-facing changes, update all relevant documentation: web app docs, CLI command references, READMEs, and SKILL files.
- Use `<table>` HTML elements instead of markdown tables in `.mdx` files in the docs app.
- Never use `--` as punctuation. Use emdashes sparingly, defaulting to commas and periods.
- Always run `pnpm type-check` at the end of each agent turn to catch type errors early.

## Contribution workflow

This repository is owner-maintained. Validate changes and push them directly to `main`. Do not create pull requests unless the owner explicitly requests one. Preserve existing work in dirty checkouts by using an isolated worktree when needed. Fetch before pushing and integrate concurrent changes without force-pushing.

## Release process

When a release is requested, keep changesets in separate commits from feature or bug-fix changes. Release preparation and version changes also go directly to `main`, without pull requests.

# yyoreel

yyoreel records scripted browser demos as MP4, GIF, or WebM with cursor animation, keystroke overlays, and sound effects. You define steps in a JSON config, and yyoreel drives headless Chrome, captures frames, and encodes with ffmpeg.

## Agent browser contract

Choose one browser mode before running `record` or `preview`:

1. If the calling environment, browser wrapper, yyork, d3k, or another tool
   provides a CDP endpoint, attach to it with `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`.
2. Otherwise, let yyoreel download and launch its isolated Chrome.

Shared Chrome is the preferred mode whenever it is already available. Use the
provider's documented status or endpoint command. Do not guess a port, start a
second Chrome, add a browser field to the yyoreel config, or translate the
endpoint into CLI flags.

Pass the endpoint only to the yyoreel process:

```bash
YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT="$cdp_endpoint" yyoreel record -c yyoreel.config.json
```

If a wrapper already injects `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`, invoke the wrapper as
documented instead of exporting another value. `WEBREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` is the
obsolete pre-rename variable and has no effect.

Attach mode creates a dedicated page target. yyoreel may close that target, but
the agent must leave the browser process and every other target running. The
configured viewport uses device emulation on yyoreel's target. It does not
resize the shared browser window.

After recording:

1. Confirm the output exists and decode it with `ffprobe` or `ffmpeg`.
2. Confirm the provider still reports its browser or CDP endpoint as healthy.
3. Report the output path and whether the shared browser survived.

## Prerequisites

Use Node.js 20.20+ on the 20.x line, or 22.22 and later.

yyoreel requires Chrome and ffmpeg. In isolated launch mode, both are automatically downloaded to `~/.yyoreel` on first run if not already present. Do not install Chrome or Chromium via puppeteer, playwright, or another browser automation tool.

In attach mode, yyoreel uses the existing Chrome and skips its Chrome download
and launch path. ffmpeg is still required for recording and composition.

To download dependencies explicitly, or to fix corrupted/broken binaries:

```bash
yyoreel install
yyoreel install --force   # delete cached binaries and re-download
```

To override the auto-downloaded binaries, set these environment variables:

- `CHROME_PATH` - path to a Chrome or Chromium binary (used for preview)
- `CHROME_HEADLESS_PATH` - path to a chrome-headless-shell binary (used for recording)
- `FFMPEG_PATH` - path to an ffmpeg binary
- `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` - existing Chrome remote debugging HTTP endpoint, WebSocket debugger URL, or port

When `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` is set, yyoreel skips Chrome download and launch,
creates a dedicated page target in the attached browser, and closes only that
target after the run. The browser remains running. The configured viewport uses
device emulation on the target and does not resize the existing browser window.
Recording features, including capture pacing, Retina quality, autozoom,
backgrounds, cursor overlays, and the HUD, use the same pipeline as launch mode.

If attach mode fails before the first step, verify the provider's endpoint is
reachable and that the wrapper passed `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`. If the browser
connects but a step fails, inspect `waitFor`, selectors, page timing, and
`--verbose` output.

## CLI commands

### init

Scaffold a new `yyoreel.config.json`.

```bash
yyoreel init
yyoreel init --name login-flow --url https://myapp.com
yyoreel init --name hero -o hero.config.json
```

Flags: `--name` (video name), `--url` (starting URL), `-o, --output` (output file path).

### record

Record one or more videos.

```bash
yyoreel record                        # all videos in config
yyoreel record hero login             # specific videos by name
yyoreel record -c custom.config.json  # custom config path
yyoreel record --watch                # re-record on config change
yyoreel record --verbose              # log each step
yyoreel record --dry-run              # print resolved config only
yyoreel record --frames               # save raw PNGs to .yyoreel/frames/
```

To record through an existing Chrome:

```bash
YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9222 yyoreel record hero
```

### preview

Run steps in a visible browser without recording.

```bash
yyoreel preview
yyoreel preview hero --verbose
```

### composite

Re-apply the recording background and overlays (cursor, HUD, sfx) to existing raw video without re-recording. Useful for tweaking theme settings.

```bash
yyoreel composite
yyoreel composite hero
```

### install

Download Chrome and ffmpeg to `~/.yyoreel`. Also use this to fix corrupted or broken binaries.

```bash
yyoreel install
yyoreel install --force  # delete cached binaries and re-download
```

### validate

Check config for errors without running anything.

```bash
yyoreel validate
yyoreel validate -c custom.config.json
```

## Config structure

Config files are auto-discovered as `yyoreel.config.json` (or `.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, `.mjs`). Use `-c` to specify a custom path.

### Top-level fields

| Field          | Default      | Description                                             |
| -------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `$schema`      | -            | `"https://yyoreel.com/schema/v1.json"`                  |
| `outDir`       | `"videos/"`  | Output directory for rendered videos                    |
| `baseUrl`      | `""`         | Base URL prepended to relative video URLs               |
| `viewport`     | main display | Usable logical area on macOS, with a 1080x1080 fallback |
| `theme`        | -            | Recording background, cursor, and HUD theme             |
| `sfx`          | -            | Sound effect settings                                   |
| `include`      | -            | Array of step file paths prepended to all videos        |
| `defaultDelay` | -            | Default delay (ms) appended after each step             |
| `clickDwell`   | -            | Cursor dwell time (ms) before a click                   |

### Per-video fields

Each entry in the `videos` map supports:

| Field          | Default        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`          | required       | URL to open (absolute or relative to `baseUrl`)    |
| `viewport`     | inherited      | Explicit dimensions or preset override             |
| `zoom`         | -              | CSS zoom factor                                    |
| `autoZoom`     | `true`         | Spring-zoom the card around related clicks         |
| `waitFor`      | -              | Selector or text to wait for before starting steps |
| `output`       | `"<name>.mp4"` | Output path (`.mp4`, `.gif`, `.webm`)              |
| `thumbnail`    | `{ time: 0 }`  | Thumbnail config, or `{ enabled: false }`          |
| `include`      | inherited      | Step files to prepend                              |
| `theme`        | inherited      | Override theme                                     |
| `sfx`          | inherited      | Override sound effects                             |
| `defaultDelay` | inherited      | Override default delay                             |
| `clickDwell`   | inherited      | Override click dwell                               |
| `fps`          | `60`           | Frame rate                                         |
| `quality`      | `80`           | Final quality and 1x or 2x physical pixel density  |
| `steps`        | required       | Array of step objects                              |

When `viewport` is omitted on macOS, yyoreel uses the main display's usable area in logical CSS pixels. Unsupported or display-less environments fall back to 1080x1080. An explicit object or named preset overrides automatic sizing.

Quality values from 80 through 100 keep the resolved CSS viewport and double the physical output width and height. Values from 1 through 79 use 1x output dimensions. If a 1x viewport has an odd dimension, yyoreel keeps its CSS layout and pads that output edge by one pixel for compatible 4:2:0 video. Automatic viewport discovery does not override this mapping. The default quality matches native density on a 2x Retina display, but density always comes from `quality`. Chrome supplies lossless PNG screencast frames. During capture, yyoreel remuxes those frames so video encoding cannot slow the output clock. Once capture stops, it compacts the retained raw with lossless ultrafast QP0 H.264 RGB while preserving the source RGB samples. A fixed output clock reuses the latest source frame when necessary to maintain the requested frame rate. For MP4 output, the final H.264 encode is the only lossy generation, using the quality-to-CRF mapping, the `veryfast` preset, and compatible 4:2:0 output. WebM and GIF exports apply their format-specific delivery encode after composition.

### Videos map

Videos are keyed by name in the config:

```json
{
  "videos": {
    "hero": { "url": "...", "steps": [...] },
    "login": { "url": "...", "steps": [...] }
  }
}
```

Record specific videos by name: `yyoreel record hero login`.

## Verified completion and voluntary feedback

Finish the complete browser flow before wrapping up. For MP4 output, wait for yyoreel's authoritative verification and `Done` output, then verify and report the exact local MP4 path to the user.

Only after verified MP4 success, ask once using this exact text:

> quick rating before we wrap: how was yyoreel? reply with 1-5, optionally followed by one category: setup, browser, recording, verification, or other.

If the user voluntarily provides a valid rating from 1 through 5, privately invoke `yyoreel feedback <rating> [category]`. Include the category only when it is exactly `setup`, `browser`, `recording`, `verification`, or `other`. Never ask for, include, persist, or transmit free text or sensitive data.

Do not block completion on a response, ask again, badger the user, or ask after a failed or non-MP4 run. Do not treat feedback as activation. Activation occurs only inside yyoreel after successful MP4 verification. Telemetry failure is silent and cannot change the recording result.

Do not promise demo, harness, data, proof, or last-mile work as part of this feedback step. Report only the verified local artifact and work actually completed.

Published packages include a write-only public PostHog project token intended for public applications. A non-empty `YYOREEL_POSTHOG_KEY` overrides it, `YYOREEL_POSTHOG_HOST` optionally overrides the ingestion host, and only `YYOREEL_TELEMETRY=0` opts out. An intentionally empty custom build with no runtime override is a no-op. The one-time `video_verified` event follows successful decoding of all optional MP4 audio and video streams and contains only yyoreel version, platform, architecture, managed or reused Chrome execution mode, and a coarse verification version. `feedback_rated` contains only the voluntary numeric rating, optional allowlisted category, and feedback prompt version. Both use a stable anonymous 32-character hexadecimal installation ID generated from 16 random bytes, an event UUID and timestamp, `$process_person_profile: false`, disabled GeoIP, and no server attribution. Delivery uses one retry-free official SDK immediate request inside a detached process with ignored stdio and a ten-second hard lifetime. The parent CLI exits promptly, and failed activation delivery stays queued for an exact retry.

## Step types

Each step has an `action` field. Most steps accept optional `label`, `delay` (ms after step), and `description` fields.

| Action       | Key fields                                  | Purpose                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `pause`      | `ms`                                        | Wait for a duration                |
| `click`      | `text` or `selector`, `within`, `modifiers` | Click an element                   |
| `type`       | `text`, `selector`, `within`, `charDelay`   | Type text into an input            |
| `key`        | `key`, `target`                             | Press a key combo (e.g. `"cmd+s"`) |
| `drag`       | `from`, `to` (element targets)              | Drag between two elements          |
| `scroll`     | `x`, `y`, `selector`                        | Scroll the page or an element      |
| `wheel`      | `deltaY`, `deltaX`, `count`, element target | Dispatch real mouse wheel events   |
| `wait`       | `selector` or `text`, `timeout`             | Wait for an element to appear      |
| `moveTo`     | `text` or `selector`, `within`              | Move cursor to an element          |
| `navigate`   | `url`                                       | Navigate to a new URL              |
| `hover`      | `text` or `selector`, `within`              | Hover over an element              |
| `select`     | `selector`, `value`                         | Select a dropdown value            |
| `screenshot` | `output`                                    | Capture a PNG screenshot           |

For full field details on every step type, see [steps-reference.md](steps-reference.md).

## Element targeting

Many steps target elements using these fields:

- `text` - match by visible text content
- `selector` - match by CSS selector
- `within` - narrow the search to a parent matching this CSS selector

You can use `text` or `selector` (not both). `within` is optional and scopes the search.

```json
{ "action": "click", "text": "Submit" }
{ "action": "click", "selector": "#submit-btn" }
{ "action": "click", "text": "Submit", "within": ".modal" }
```

## Viewport presets

Use preset names as string values for `viewport`, or specify `{ width, height }`. Both forms override automatic display sizing:

`desktop` (1920x1080), `desktop-hd` (2560x1440), `laptop` (1366x768), `macbook-air` (1440x900), `macbook-pro` (1512x982), `ipad` (1024x1366), `ipad-pro` (834x1194), `ipad-mini` (768x1024), `iphone-15` (393x852), `iphone-15-pro-max` (430x932), `iphone-se` (375x667), `pixel-8` (412x915), `galaxy-s24` (360x780).

## Vault: what it protects, and what it does not

The credential vault **exists at the audited pinned commit**. It is not a feature assumed from a newer branch.

- The local encrypted store is `<get_hermes_home()>/vault`, with a key and encrypted file. Item metadata contains ID, kind, label, origin, identifier and dates, but no Slack user/owner or conversation audience field (`agent/vault_store.py:153-173,193-201,355-375`).
- `browser_vault_list` walks all enabled backends and returns every available item’s non-secret metadata; it receives no authenticated owner input (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:221-259,710-711`). A local backend is always included (`agent/vault_backends/base.py:125-139`).
- `browser_vault_fill` accepts a handle, resolves it in the current profile’s backends, checks the saved origin, then injects into the current task’s browser. It does not check the Slack sender or require that the task that saved the item is the one using it (`tools/browser_vault_tool.py:400-479,521-569`). This is the correct design for one personal profile reused across its owner's sessions, but not for several independent owners in one profile.
- Passwords are withheld from ordinary model tool outputs. Exact-origin checks, an in-page recheck, server-side secret injection, and redaction are real protections. **These protect password handling; they do not authorize which human may use the account.** Someone can improperly act through a login without seeing the password.
- External password-manager unlock tokens are keyed by `(Hermes home, backend)` (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:65-104`). The `owner_session` field only decides which session teardown removes the token (`113-141`); it is not checked when another session fetches the token. Same-profile sessions can reuse an existing unlock. Different-profile tokens are separated.
- 1Password service tokens and Connect credentials use the current profile's secret scope; the configured account may differ by profile (`agent/vault_backends/onepassword.py:36-40,50-68`). Managers list login items available to their configured manager account rather than applying a Slack-owner filter (`101-124`; `agent/vault_backends/bitwarden.py:88-124`). Bitwarden’s CLI home/appdata environment comes from the host (`28-29,48-53`), so separate token slots do not by themselves configure distinct Bitwarden accounts for separate reviewers.

The docs accurately state local vault scope is the profile (`website/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault.md:87-90`), and describe the model-blind origin-binding guarantee (`110-122`). They do not promise per-Slack-user account authorization.

## Related secure input finding

Messaging `gateway/` contains no registration of the vault unlock/save-login/code callbacks. Registration exists in CLI chat and TUI/Desktop bridges (`hermes_cli/cli_chat_turn_mixin.py:312-319`; `tui_gateway/agent_callbacks.py:216-232`). The messaging turn runner registers the ordinary gateway approval callback, not these vault callbacks (`gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1688-1728`). `can_prompt_here()` requires the vault unlock callback (`agent/vault_backends/unlock.py:162-171`). Therefore stock Slack should not be assumed to have the documented masked credential dialog. Saved local credentials can still be used by that profile. A secure web handoff or an appropriate callback bridge is needed for the reviewer collection experience; no new vault cryptography is implied.

## Local probes and limits

Reproducible source: [probes/browser_vault_ownership.py](probes/browser_vault_ownership.py). Captured successful invocation and output: [evidence/browser_vault_ownership.json](evidence/browser_vault_ownership.json).

A temporary Python process created three disposable Hermes homes, disabled external managers in dummy config, and used real imports. Dummy records were added through `VaultStore.add_item`; list and fill functions were the real implementations. Only page inspection/injection functions were mocked to prevent browser/network use. It checked these outcomes, all true:

| Probe | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| DM-B task lists DM-A dummy vault metadata in same profile | Allowed |
| DM-B reaches the secret-fill boundary using A's handle on the matching dummy origin | Allowed; injection received B's task ID and A's dummy secret |
| Different profile lists A's local vault entry | Denied by separate store; list empty |
| DM-B reuses A's dummy Bitwarden token in same profile | Allowed |
| Different profile reuses A's dummy manager token | No token |
| Different task IDs plus same named Browser Use session within a profile | Same backend cache key |
| Same name under different profile homes | Different backend cache keys |
| Unnamed Browser Use backend keys for different task IDs | Different keys; this does not certify external harness default-daemon isolation |
| Camofox managed identities for A/B tasks in one profile | Same user ID, different session keys |
| Camofox managed identities under different profiles | Different user IDs |
| Real-profile cached CDP endpoint queried under profile A then B, both enabled | Same endpoint returned |

The real-profile probe pre-seeded a dummy cached endpoint and mocked healthcheck/socket-directory preparation. It demonstrates the profile-unkeyed cache path, not a live cross-account browser theft. The vault fill probe demonstrates the missing owner check and successful traversal to the injection boundary, not successful login to a real website. No live Slack/browser E2E has been completed by these probes.

Relevant existing upstream tests cover exact-origin rejection, secret-free return values, race rechecks and file guards (`tests/tools/test_browser_vault.py`), profile-scoped external token storage and teardown ownership (`tests/agent/test_vault_backends.py:139-170`), and profile-keyed Browser Use backend caches (`tests/tools/test_browser_computer_use_profile_cache_keys.py:28-46`). Their intended assertions do not establish two-user authorization inside one profile.

## Smallest justified next design

1. Route each authenticated owner’s private DM to its own Hermes profile; route shared channels/threads to a separate audience profile without private owner credentials. Reuse native profile vaults and secret scopes. This establishes logical ownership for the reviewed profile-scoped paths.
2. Force browser session names/identities from trusted runtime context rather than model-chosen owner/session IDs. A thin integration can namespace each logical browser session by the authorized profile and owner; a browser service can reject any foreign identifier. Keep private persistent browser contexts separately bound to that authority.
3. Keep `browser.use_real_profile` off in the shared process; avoid a shared/global CDP endpoint. Use explicitly isolated browser contexts/services or fix the real-profile cache and prove the relevant backend behavior. Camofox persistence can reuse owner profile identities if its server truly enforces them.
4. Decide the execution boundary from enabled capabilities. `browser_exec` runs arbitrary **host** Python (`model_tools.py:391-395`; its actual dispatch is a host subprocess in `tools/browser_use_cli.py:612-662`). A Docker-only terminal setting does not establish isolation for this path. Options include whole-runtime OS/container isolation, or disabling host-code-capable tools and using a constrained browser broker plus storage/credential ACLs. Merely naming profiles is insufficient for hostile direct resource attempts.
5. Test two private owners plus one shared audience with dummy markers against those exact tools and settings, including named browser-session collision, matching-origin foreign vault use, persistent cookies, same-process profile transitions, concurrent actions, and restart. Treat only verified backend behavior as accepted.

**Verified outcome: stock same-profile browser/vault scope fails the requested private-owner boundary; routed profiles reuse substantial existing machinery, but the selected browser and execution path still require explicit enforcement and live acceptance.**
"""Offline, dummy-only ownership probe. No live browser or network calls.

Run with the pinned Hermes venv Python. Real vault/profile/key functions execute;
only browser page inspection, secret injection, and real-profile cache health
checks are mocked. All test homes are temporary and removed on exit.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
upstream = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".local/hermes-lab/upstream"
sys.path.insert(0, str(upstream))


def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="clanker-browser-audit-") as tmp:
        root = Path(tmp)
        os.environ["HERMES_HOME"] = str(root / "launch")
        for name in ("launch", "owner_a", "owner_b"):
            home = root / name
            home.mkdir()
            (home / "config.yaml").write_text(
                "vault:\n  onepassword:\n    enabled: false\n  bitwarden:\n    enabled: false\n"
                "browser:\n  use_real_profile: true\n  cloud_provider: local\n"
            )
        from hermes_constants import set_hermes_home_override, reset_hermes_home_override
        from agent.vault_store import get_vault_store
        from agent.vault_backends import unlock
        from tools import browser_vault_tool as vt, browser_use_cli as bu, browser_tool as bt
        from tools.browser_camofox_state import get_camofox_identity
        from tools import browser_tool_real_profile as rp

        @contextmanager
        def scope(name):
            token = set_hermes_home_override(root / name)
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                reset_hermes_home_override(token)

        out = {}
        with scope("owner_a"):
            unlock.set_current_session_id("slack-dm-A")
            meta = get_vault_store().add_item(
                "login", "Owner A dummy",
                {"identifier_type": "email", "identifier": "owner-a@example.test",
                 "password": "REDACTED"}, "https://example.test"
            )
            listed_a = json.loads(vt._handle_vault_list({}, task_id="slack-dm-A"))["items"]
            unlock.store_session_token("bitwarden", "dummy-manager-token")
            unlock.set_current_session_id("slack-dm-B")
            listed_b = json.loads(vt._handle_vault_list({}, task_id="slack-dm-B"))["items"]
            out["same_profile_vault_metadata_visible_to_other_task"] = listed_a == listed_b and len(listed_b) == 1
            out["same_profile_unlock_reused_by_other_session"] = unlock.get_session_token("bitwarden") == "dummy-manager-token"
            out["same_profile_named_browser_key_collision"] = bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-A", "work") == bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-B", "work")
            out["different_tasks_unnamed_browser_keys_differ"] = bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-A") != bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-B")
            key_a = bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-A", "work")
            camo_a = get_camofox_identity("slack-dm-A")
            camo_b = get_camofox_identity("slack-dm-B")
            out["same_profile_camofox_tasks_share_user_id"] = camo_a["user_id"] == camo_b["user_id"]
            out["same_profile_camofox_tasks_have_distinct_session_keys"] = camo_a["session_key"] != camo_b["session_key"]
            injected = []
            controls = [{"autocomplete": "current-password", "formIndex": 0, "index": 0,
                         "label": "", "name": "pw", "type": "password"}]

            def dummy_eval(task_id, expression):
                return {"success": True, "result": "https://example.test/login"
                        if "location.href" in expression else json.dumps(controls)}

            def dummy_secret_eval(task_id, expression):
                injected.append((task_id, "REDACTED" in expression))
                return {"success": True, "result": json.dumps({"filled": 1})}

            with patch.object(vt, "_focus_bound_origin", return_value=None), \
                 patch.object(vt, "_eval_js", side_effect=dummy_eval), \
                 patch.object(vt, "_eval_js_secret", side_effect=dummy_secret_eval):
                result = json.loads(vt.browser_vault_fill(meta.id, task_id="slack-dm-B"))
            out["other_task_can_reach_secret_fill_boundary"] = result["success"] and injected == [("slack-dm-B", True)]

        with scope("owner_b"):
            out["different_profile_vault_empty"] = json.loads(vt._handle_vault_list({}, task_id="slack-dm-B"))["items"] == []
            out["different_profile_unlock_not_reused"] = unlock.get_session_token("bitwarden") is None
            out["different_profile_named_browser_keys_differ"] = key_a != bu._backend_cache_key("slack-dm-B", "work")
            out["different_profile_camofox_user_ids_differ"] = camo_a["user_id"] != get_camofox_identity("slack-dm-B")["user_id"]

        with patch.object(rp._cloud, "_use_real_profile", return_value=True), \
             patch.object(rp._lp, "_using_lightpanda_engine", return_value=False), \
             patch.object(rp, "_cdp_http_ready", return_value=True), \
             patch.object(rp._session, "_prepare_session_socket_dir", return_value=str(root / "sockets")):
            with scope("owner_a"):
                bt._real_profile_cdp_cache["cdp"] = "http://127.0.0.1:12345/dummy-owner-a"
                real_a = rp._real_profile_cdp()
            with scope("owner_b"):
                real_b = rp._real_profile_cdp()
            out["cached_real_profile_cdp_reused_across_profiles"] = real_a == real_b == ("http://127.0.0.1:12345/dummy-owner-a", None)

        bt._real_profile_cdp_cache.clear()
        unlock.lock_all_profiles()
        print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
        assert all(out.values()), "An expected scope observation changed; inspect the output."


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Step types reference

Every step object requires an `action` field. Most steps also accept these optional fields:

- `label` (string) - display label for the keystroke HUD overlay
- `delay` (number) - milliseconds to wait after the step completes
- `description` (string) - human-readable note (not used at runtime)

## Element targeting

Several steps target DOM elements via these fields:

- `text` (string) - match by visible text content
- `selector` (string) - match by CSS selector
- `within` (string) - CSS selector to scope the search to a parent element

Use `text` or `selector`, not both. `within` is always optional.

---

## pause

Wait for a fixed duration.

| Field    | Type      | Required | Description              |
| -------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------ |
| `action` | `"pause"` | yes      |                          |
| `ms`     | number    | yes      | Duration in milliseconds |

```json
{ "action": "pause", "ms": 500 }
```

## click

Click a DOM element.

| Field       | Type      | Required | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `action`    | `"click"` | yes      |                                                               |
| `text`      | string    | no       | Match element by visible text                                 |
| `selector`  | string    | no       | Match element by CSS selector                                 |
| `within`    | string    | no       | Scope search to a parent selector                             |
| `modifiers` | string[]  | no       | Modifier keys held during click (e.g. `["shift"]`, `["cmd"]`) |

Provide `text` or `selector` (at least one).

```json
{ "action": "click", "text": "Submit" }
{ "action": "click", "selector": "#save-btn", "delay": 500 }
{ "action": "click", "text": "Item 3", "modifiers": ["shift"] }
{ "action": "click", "text": "Delete", "within": ".modal" }
```

## type

Type text into an input element. If no target is specified, types into the currently focused element.

| Field       | Type     | Required | Description                         |
| ----------- | -------- | -------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `action`    | `"type"` | yes      |                                     |
| `text`      | string   | yes      | Text to type                        |
| `selector`  | string   | no       | Target input by CSS selector        |
| `within`    | string   | no       | Scope search to a parent selector   |
| `charDelay` | number   | no       | Milliseconds between each character |

```json
{ "action": "type", "text": "user@example.com", "selector": "#email", "charDelay": 40 }
```

## key

Press a keyboard shortcut or key combination.

| Field    | Type                    | Required | Description                      |
| -------- | ----------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------- |
| `action` | `"key"`                 | yes      |                                  |
| `key`    | string                  | yes      | Key or combo string              |
| `target` | string or ElementTarget | no       | Element to focus before pressing |

Key combo syntax uses `+` to join modifiers: `"cmd+s"`, `"ctrl+shift+p"`, `"alt+tab"`, `"Enter"`, `"Escape"`, `"ArrowDown"`.

Modifier names: `cmd`, `ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `meta`.

```json
{ "action": "key", "key": "cmd+s" }
{ "action": "key", "key": "Enter", "delay": 500 }
{ "action": "key", "key": "ctrl+shift+p", "label": "Command Palette" }
```

## drag

Drag from one element to another.
